annotations.title: Be told when the answer about an address changes

description: Ask to be told when the answer about an address CHANGES. The dimensions are the ones the counterparty check already answers, so this is that same reading on a schedule rather than a second opinion; what it adds is the comparison. The first run records a reading and reports nothing — there is nothing yet to compare against, and a first reading dressed up as news is the thing this avoids. Idempotent per subject: calling it again edits the watch rather than creating a second. An unknown dimension or policy is REFUSED rather than dropped, because a watch that quietly ignores half of what you asked for is worse than no watch. Needs a key. WHY readOnlyHint IS false: this call writes a row in our store on behalf of the caller, so a second identical call is not free of consequence.

dimensions.description: What to watch. All four if you leave it out. An unknown name is refused, not ignored.

policy.description: The policy its verdict is read against. An unknown name is refused rather than replaced with a default.

name: monitor_subject

answerLead.description: SINCE 2026-11-28: at most three lines before the full answer, from its own fields: `text`, `result`, `risks` (up to two), `asOf`, `coverage`, `unknowns` (up to two) and `deprecatedFields` (legacy duplicates this answer still carries). The full answer governs. Added by this MCP server; the REST route behind the tool does not carry it.

dimensions.description: What is actually being watched, which is what you asked for or all four.

firstReadingAt.description: When the comparison baseline was taken. Null means no reading yet, so nothing can be reported as a change.

id.description: The watch, for changing or ending it later.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

policy.description: The policy its verdict is read against. Null where the watch names none and the default applies; read `says` for which that is.

says.description: What this watch will and will not tell you. It reports a CHANGE in what we hold, which is not the same as a change in the world.

subject.description: The address being watched, read back so a watch cannot be set on the wrong one.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it, each {code, message, says} with message and says the same sentence. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.

title: Be told when the answer about an address changes
